open_points.subject: execute_function descriptor inheritance
open_points.text: each trap first writes its hit to a channel to the parent that the code cannot unsend
open_points.other_text: Every descriptor the environment needs from the parent — the write end of the trap channel, the --info-fd pipe — reaches bubblewrap by inheritance, passed with subprocess pass_fds, and bubblewrap keeps it open for the child: bubblewrap has no option that names a descriptor to keep, and --preserve-fds does not exist.
open_points.question: The trap channel must reach the sandboxed child, but subprocess pass_fds preserves it only into bubblewrap; bubblewrap must explicitly preserve it for the child, using its --preserve-fds option. Must the instruction denying that option change, or must another supported descriptor-passing mechanism be specified?
